required_own_edits.source_excerpt: For every integer $k\ge1$, let $U_k\subset S^3$ be a $k$-component planar unlink with an arbitrary orientation on each component, and choose a basepoint $p$ on any one component. Its double branched cover is $\#^{\,k-1}(S^2\times S^1)$, with $\Sigma(U_1)=S^3$. Over $\mathbb F_2$, the hat Floer group of this cover is identified with the exterior algebra on a $(k-1)$-dimensional vector space, hence has rank $2^{k-1}$. Under these identifications, the cobordism maps for saddle cobordisms between neighboring unlink resolutions, with $p$ carried outside the saddle disk, are the multiplication and comultiplication maps of the two-dimensional Frobenius algebra $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$ after reduction at the marked component. The identification includes the marked-circle cases and fixes the basis conventions needed to compare the first surgery differential with the reduced Khovanov cube.

required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: The cover is constructed by crosswise gluing two labeled copies of the cut balls along the finitely many bridge disks, using $(s,z)\mapsto(s,z^2)$ along the branch arcs and the matching endpoint charts. These charts give its orientation and smooth structure directly. Thus this is a finite realization of the local branch convention in [F1], without invoking the generic AC-dependent covering classification or any Floer map.

operations.source_excerpt: Fix a finite regular diagram $D$ of a nonempty oriented link $L\subset S^3$, choose a basepoint $p\in D$ away from the crossings, and choose an admissible pointed Heegaard multi-diagram subordinate to the branched-cover surgeries, with the compatible perturbation data and top-generator cycles of the link-surgery construction. Identify each first-page vertex group with the reduced state space of the corresponding crossingless resolution, based at the circle containing $p$. For every cube edge, the induced first differential is the mod-two map assigned by the saddle: multiplication when two resolution circles merge and comultiplication when one resolution circle splits, with the marked-circle quotient at $p$. Under these identifications the direct sum of edge maps is the reduced Khovanov differential of the mirror diagram $\overline D$, based at the corresponding point, in the Ozsváth–Szabó smoothing convention.
